content:
As part of our Live Project with WeiKFiELD Foods Pvt Ltd, my team and I spent 10 days at a Reliance Smart Superstore observing how a product performs once it reaches the shelf.

The experience went beyond selling. It showed how much shelf placement, stock rotation, and visibility influence whether a product actually gets picked up.

Even well-established products can go unnoticed if placement isn't right. Newer stock often moves faster than older stock simply because rotation wasn't managed well and visibility alone doesn't guarantee a sale, what a product sits next to matters just as much.

Distribution doesn't end when a product reaches the store. What happens on the shelf after that determines whether it sells at all.

Grateful to have worked on this alongside my teammates Jayshree, Ritu Bishwakarma, Saara, Aditi Verma and Vartika Srivastava figuring this out together made the experience even better.
comment: The shelf is often the final mile of brand strategy. Small factors like planogram data, replenishment timing, and retailer execution can decide whether consumer intent turns into an actual purchase.
